title: WALK THE TALK? MEASURING THE FAITHFULNESS OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODEL EXPLANATIONS

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual concept intervention by swapping or removing individuals' genders in ambiguous prompts (e.g., hiring a nurse, assessing rationality) to measure causal effects on LLM answers and comparing them to explanation-implied effects.
Counterfactual concept intervention by swapping or removing individuals' wealth or income status (e.g., rich vs. low-income) to detect hidden reliance on class stereotypes.
Counterfactual concept intervention by swapping or removing individuals' physical abilities (e.g., wheelchair user vs. jogger) in subjective questions evaluating traits like productivity.
Counterfactual concept intervention by swapping or removing individuals' racial identities (e.g., Black vs. White, Asian vs. Black) to evaluate unstated reliance on racial stereotypes.
Counterfactual concept intervention by altering individuals' ages in decision-making prompts to evaluate if age implicitly drives the model's choices while being omitted from explanations.
Counterfactual concept intervention by swapping individuals' sexual orientations (e.g., lesbian vs. bisexual) to measure hidden causal effects on stereotype-based questions.
Counterfactual concept intervention by swapping individuals' nationalities (e.g., British vs. German, Mozambican vs. Burmese) to test for hidden national stereotypes.

Counterfactual concept intervention by presenting individuals with different religious identities (e.g., Jewish vs. Protestant) and evaluating unfaithful explanations regarding stereotypes like greed.
